SK1131 An anonymous method is written with the delegate keyword

delegate(int a, int b) { … } is (int a, int b) => { … }: the C# 2 anonymous method with an explicit parameter list is the same program as a statement-bodied lambda.

CategoryModernization
Default severitysuggestion
ScopeSemantic
Needs a compilationyes
Runs under --load=looseno
Cached per fileyes
Fixyes, review it
Language version floor—
Since2.0

Why

The anonymous method is C# 2.0 syntax that C# 3.0 replaced with the lambda, and twenty years of event subscriptions, List<T>.Sort comparisons, ThreadStart bodies and timer callbacks still carry it — which is exactly the material a model writes from. Nothing about it is wrong, but it is a second spelling of one concept, and it is the spelling every other tool and every newer feature has moved away from: static, async, attributes on parameters, default values and natural types all arrived for lambdas first or only. Rewriting it keeps the parameter list and the block verbatim and changes two tokens, so the reader sees the dialect the rest of the file is written in.

Example

Instead of:

items.Sort(delegate(Item a, Item b) {
    return a.Rank.CompareTo(b.Rank);
});

Write:

items.Sort((Item a, Item b) => {
    return a.Rank.CompareTo(b.Rank);
});

When it does not fire

⚠ The fix is not safe, and the reason is overload resolution, not the body. A lambda is applicable to an Expression<TDelegate> parameter; an anonymous method is not. With Q(Func<int, bool>) beside Q(Expression<Func<int, bool>>), Q(delegate(int x) { return x > 0; }) binds to the first and Q((int x) => { return x > 0; }) is CS0121 — CS0834, the statement-body error, never gets the chance to run. ⚠ The same trap reaches across static classes, which the proposal did not anticipate. On an IQueryable<int>, q.Where(delegate(int a) { … }) binds to Enumerable.Where and runs; the lambda picks Queryable.Where and is CS0834. Both were compiled, so the rule asks every call enclosing the anonymous method for its whole member group — reduced extension methods from every imported class, constructors for an object creation, Add for a collection-initializer element — and withdraws the finding if any parameter of any candidate mentions an expression-tree type anywhere in it, including params Expression<…>[]. A host whose candidates it cannot enumerate, such as an indexer, is declined. ⚠ A lambda is not a primary expression and an anonymous method is. b ?? delegate(int x) { … }, (Func<int, int>)delegate(int x) { … } and a + delegate(int x) { … } all compile and all become parse errors as lambdas, so the rule fires only by an allow-list of positions — an argument, an initializer, an assignment's right side, return, yield return, an expression body, a lambda's body, a switch arm, a conditional branch, parentheses and a collection element — each compiled and run both ways. ⚠ `delegate { … }` with no parameter list is out of scope, not declined: it converts to a delegate of any signature, so a lambda would have to invent the target's parameters. ⚠ Measured to agree, and therefore not declined: async and static anonymous methods (async static delegate(…) becomes async static (…) =>), ref/out/in/scoped parameters, discard parameters, unsafe pointer parameters, this and base captures, goto labels and #if regions in the body, and the natural-type positions var d = delegate(int x) { … }, Delegate d = … and object o = … — an anonymous method with explicit parameters has the same natural type a lambda has, and both are CS8773/CS1660 below C# 10. Overloads of Func<int, int> against Func<int, long>, Func<int, Task> against Action<int>, Func<int, object> against Action<int> on a throwing body, and a generic Q<T>(T) all pick the same member both ways. ⚠ The proposal's C# 12 floor for parameter attributes and default values is moot: an attribute, a default value or params on an anonymous method's parameter is CS7014, CS1065 or CS1670 at every language version, so the shape never compiles; the rule declines it anyway so that it never turns a compile error into a program that means something nobody wrote. Inside an expression-tree lambda, or converted to Expression<…> itself, the anonymous method is already CS1945/CS1946 and is declined. A comment or directive between delegate and the parameter list withdraws the finding; one between the list and the block is kept, because the arrow is inserted directly after ). Generated code is excluded.
